newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-SIDHU WITHIN DOUBLE CENTURY AS INDIA TAKE CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU WITHIN DOUBLE CENTURY AS INDIA TAKE CHARGE.

text.p: Opener Navjot Sidhu moved within four runs of a memorable double century on Sunday as he helped put India in an almost impregnable position in the second test against the West Indies.

Sidhu, who began the day on 102, moved to a career-best 196 not out as India reached a healthy 367 for three at the close on the third day in reply to the West Indies's first innings total of 296 all out.
However, while it is now nearly impossible for India to lose the match, Sunday's slow progress means that a draw now looks the most likely result.

Captain Sachin Tendulkar lent valuable support with an innings of 88 in five hours as he and Sidhu, whose ten-and-a-half hour innings has included one six and 19 fours, put on 174 runs for the third wicket.

The pair, batting on the ground where India recorded their last test victory in the Caribbean 21 years ago, had been in debt to the Indian team after making just 32 runs between them in the first test.

Sidhu's international career appeared to have ended when he walked out on the squad in England last year but India's difficulty in finding a reliable opening partnership meant that he got another chance.
He is now poised to join Sunil Gavaskar and Dilip Sardesal as the only Indians to make double centuries against the West Indies.

Sidhu earned reprieves on 170 when wicketkeeper Junior Murray dropped him off fast bowler Mervyn Dillon and four runs later when he drove a delivery from Shivnarine Chanderpaul through the hands of Franklyn Rose.
The day had begun badly for India, who resumed on 171 for two overnight, when they lost Rahul Dravid, bowled by Curtly Ambrose for 57 off the third ball of the day, without adding to their score.
But Dravid's downfall brought Tendulkar and Sidhu together and the West Indies' problems were only begining.

Searching for form and confidence, the captain was studious in his almost impeccable knock which contained eight fours. He was eventually run out while attempting a cheeky single, West Indian captain Courtney Walsh hitting the stumps from mid-off with Tendulkar stranded.
Incoming batsman Saurav Ganguly took 38 minutes and 23 balls to get off the mark and was three not out at the close.
The West Indies bowlers showed commitment but gained little from the pitch which has been criticised for its benign nature. Ambrose was the pick with two for 71.
